title: TV Size to Viewing Distance Chart: 43 to 150-Inch Screens
metaDescription: Sit about 6 ft 6 in from a 65-inch TV and 12 ft from a 120-inch screen (THX 40°). Viewing distance chart for 43 to 150 inches, plus screen size by seat.
h1: TV Size to Viewing Distance Chart
keywords: what size tv for my room
how far to sit from a 65 inch tv
intro:
For a cinema-like view, sit about **1.2 times the screen diagonal** away: **6 ft 6 in from a 65-inch TV**, 7 ft 6 in from a 75-inch and 12 ft from a 120-inch projector screen. That is the THX recommendation of a screen filling about 40 degrees of your field of view. The SMPTE minimum of 30 degrees puts you about 1.6 times the diagonal away.

The chart below gives both, plus the distance at which 4K and 1080p detail stops being visible to 20/20 eyes, and a reverse table that turns your seat distance into a screen size. Every figure is calculated from the angles, so it works for TVs and projector screens alike. For any size not listed, use our [viewing distance calculator](/tools/viewing-distance-calculator/).
quickAnswer: Multiply the diagonal by **1.2** for the THX 40-degree view or by **1.6** for the SMPTE 30-degree minimum. A 65-inch TV: 6 ft 6 in (THX) to 8 ft 10 in (SMPTE). A 75-inch: 7 ft 6 in to 10 ft 2 in. A 100-inch screen: 10 ft to 13 ft 7 in. To pick a size from your seat, divide the distance in inches by 1.2.

sections.heading: TV size viewing distance chart
sections.body:
Distances are from your eyes to the screen, for 16:9 screens. The detail columns show how close you must sit to see every pixel with 20/20 vision (one arcminute per pixel); sit farther and the extra resolution is hard to see.

| Screen size | THX 40° (ideal) | SMPTE 30° (minimum) | 4K detail limit | 1080p detail limit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 43-inch | 4 ft 3 in | 5 ft 10 in | 2 ft 10 in | 5 ft 7 in |
| 50-inch | 5 ft 0 in | 6 ft 9 in | 3 ft 3 in | 6 ft 6 in |
| 55-inch | 5 ft 6 in | 7 ft 5 in | 3 ft 7 in | 7 ft 2 in |
| 65-inch | 6 ft 6 in | 8 ft 10 in | 4 ft 3 in | 8 ft 5 in |
| 75-inch | 7 ft 6 in | 10 ft 2 in | 4 ft 11 in | 9 ft 9 in |
| 85-inch | 8 ft 6 in | 11 ft 6 in | 5 ft 6 in | 11 ft 1 in |
| 98-inch | 9 ft 9 in | 13 ft 3 in | 6 ft 4 in | 12 ft 9 in |
| 100-inch | 10 ft 0 in | 13 ft 7 in | 6 ft 6 in | 13 ft 0 in |
| 120-inch | 12 ft 0 in | 16 ft 3 in | 7 ft 10 in | 15 ft 7 in |
| 135-inch | 13 ft 6 in | 18 ft 4 in | 8 ft 9 in | 17 ft 7 in |
| 150-inch | 15 ft 0 in | 20 ft 4 in | 9 ft 9 in | 19 ft 6 in |

Read it two ways. Between the THX and SMPTE columns is the comfortable range for films. If you sit beyond the 4K detail limit, which most living rooms do, a 4K TV still looks cleaner thanks to better processing and HDR, but a bigger screen adds more than more pixels.

sections.heading: What size TV or screen should I get for my seating distance?
sections.body:
Measure from the main seat to where the screen will hang, then read across.

| Seat distance | THX 40° size | SMPTE 30° size |
|---|---|---|
| 5 ft | 50-inch | 37-inch |
| 6 ft | 60-inch | 44-inch |
| 7 ft | 70-inch | 52-inch |
| 8 ft | 80-inch | 59-inch |
| 9 ft | 90-inch | 66-inch |
| 10 ft | 100-inch | 74-inch |
| 11 ft | 110-inch | 81-inch |
| 12 ft | 120-inch | 89-inch |
| 13 ft | 130-inch | 96-inch |
| 14 ft | 140-inch | 103-inch |
| 16 ft | 160-inch | 118-inch |

TVs come in fixed sizes, so round down to the nearest model. At 9 feet, the THX answer is about 90 inches; an 85-inch TV is the realistic pick, and a 75-inch sits closer to the SMPTE guide.

sections.heading: Where do the THX and SMPTE numbers come from?
sections.body:
**SMPTE**, the film and TV engineering body, gives 30 degrees as a minimum viewing angle for a theater-like experience. **THX** recommends about 40 degrees for the ideal seat. The maths for a 16:9 screen:

- Screen width = diagonal × 0.8716.
- Distance = (width ÷ 2) ÷ tan(half the angle).
- At 40°, that is width × 1.374, or about **diagonal × 1.2**. At 30°, width × 1.866, or about **diagonal × 1.63**.

Neither is a rule. Gamers and sports fans often sit nearer the SMPTE line, film fans nearer THX or closer.

sections.heading: How far should you sit from a 4K TV?
sections.body: To resolve every pixel of a 4K screen with 20/20 vision, sit within about **0.78 times the diagonal**: 4 ft 3 in for a 65-inch, 4 ft 11 in for a 75-inch. For 1080p it is about 1.56 times. Most sofas are farther than the 4K line, which is why screen size matters more than resolution at normal distances. The benefits of 4K that do not depend on distance, like [HDR](/glossary/hdr/) and better colour, still show.

sections.heading: How high should a TV be mounted?
sections.body: A common guide is to put the centre of the screen near seated eye height, about 40 to 42 inches from the floor for most sofas. Higher mounting, such as above a fireplace, tilts your head back; if you must, use a tilting or pull-down mount. Projector screens are usually mounted higher because they are bigger, with the bottom edge above the heads of any front row.

sections.heading: Does viewing distance change for projector screens?
sections.body: The angles are the same; only the sizes are bigger. A 120-inch screen at 12 feet gives the THX view; at 16 ft 3 in it is the SMPTE minimum. Once you have a size, check how far back the projector must sit in our [projector throw distance chart](/projector-throw-distance-chart/).

sections.heading: Which TVs come in the sizes on this chart?
sections.body: From the models we track: the [Hisense U8QG](/gear/hisense-u8qg/) is listed from 55 to 100 inches and the [TCL QM7K](/gear/tcl-qm7k/) from 55 to 98 inches, so both cover the large sizes the THX column asks for in most living rooms. The [LG C5 OLED](/gear/lg-c5-oled/) runs 42 to 83 inches. See the [best TV for home theater](/best-tv-for-home-theater/) for picks by room.

mistakes.title: Measuring from the wall instead of your eyes
mistakes.body: Measure from where your head sits on the sofa. A deep sofa can add a foot or more.

mistakes.title: Buying for resolution instead of size
mistakes.body: At normal distances most people cannot resolve 4K detail on smaller screens. Going one size up usually changes more than a resolution upgrade.

mistakes.title: Ignoring the second row
mistakes.body: In a dedicated room, size the screen for the main row and check the back row still clears the SMPTE 30-degree line.

mistakes.title: Mounting too high
mistakes.body: A screen centred well above eye level is tiring over a two-hour film. Keep the centre near seated eye height.

faqs.q: How far should you sit from a 65-inch TV?
faqs.a: About 6 ft 6 in for the THX 40-degree view and up to 8 ft 10 in for the SMPTE 30-degree minimum. To see every 4K pixel with 20/20 vision you would need to be within about 4 ft 3 in.

faqs.q: How far should you sit from a 75-inch TV?
faqs.a: About 7 ft 6 in (THX) to 10 ft 2 in (SMPTE). The 4K full-detail distance is about 4 ft 11 in.

faqs.q: What size TV for a 10-foot viewing distance?
faqs.a: About 100 inches for the THX 40-degree view or 74 inches for the SMPTE minimum. In TV sizes, that means 75 to 98 inches, depending on how cinematic you want it.

faqs.q: What size TV for an 8-foot distance?
faqs.a: About 80 inches by THX and 59 inches by SMPTE. A 65- or 75-inch TV is a good fit for most 8-foot rooms.

faqs.q: Can you sit too close to a TV?
faqs.a: It will not harm your eyes, but if the screen fills much more than 40 degrees you turn your head to follow action, and lower-quality sources show their flaws. Sit where the whole picture fits comfortably in view.

faqs.q: Is viewing distance different for 4K and 8K?
faqs.a: The comfort angles are the same. Higher resolution only lets you sit closer before seeing pixels: about 0.78 times the diagonal for 4K, half that for 8K.

bottomLine:
Sit about **1.2 times the diagonal** away for the THX 40-degree view and no more than about **1.6 times** for the SMPTE 30-degree minimum: 6 ft 6 in to 8 ft 10 in for a 65-inch TV, 12 to 16 feet for a 120-inch screen. Work backward from your sofa with the reverse table, then pick a TV from the [best TV for home theater](/best-tv-for-home-theater/) or plan a projector with the [throw distance chart](/projector-throw-distance-chart/). The [home theater setup guide](/home-theater-setup-guide/) covers the rest of the room.

Once you know the distance, [our home theater seating picks](/best-home-theater-seating/) cover the reclined depth each chair needs.
